## 2026-11-14 — executor — B336 portal travel and linking

What
- New `registry/portal/PortalTravel` (ADR 0077 D6, clean room): `MsmPortalBlock.getPortalDestination` now hands travellers to vanilla's portal pipeline. Target level: `return_to` from `destination`, else `destination` (also from a third dimension). Factor: with `travel.scale`, `1 / scale` going to `destination` and `scale` coming back; otherwise (and from a third dimension) `DimensionType.getTeleportationScale`. Target block: the traveller's x and z times the factor (y kept), clamped to the target's world border. Linking radius `clamp(round(128 * min(1, factor)), 16, 128)`; exits through B333's `ExitPortals.findOrBuild` with the entry's axis; the traveller keeps its share of the portal's width and height (vanilla's generic `PortalShape.getRelativePosition` and `findCollisionFreePosition`) and its rotation (a quarter turn when the exit has the other axis). `arrival: surface` lands on the first standing spot of the target column from the top of the logical height down and builds nothing; over a void it falls back to an exit. A tag frame without `frame_block` arrives at the surface (at the target itself over a void).
- The entry portal joins the index on first use when it stands in a whole lit frame (portals placed by `/fill`, structures or other mods); a lone portal block takes travellers but is not indexed.
- After arrival: `PLACE_PORTAL_TICKET`; `PLAY_PORTAL_SOUND` for the default travel sound, a project or other sound sent to a travelling player (volume 0.25, pitch 0.8 to 1.2), nothing for `false`; `cooldown_ticks` set on the arrived entity, and kept by the portal block while a cooling entity stands in it (vanilla would refresh it to its own default); then `on_travel` with the traveller as self and other at its arrival block (`run_function` runs as the traveller).
- Missing levels: `MsmRegistrar.checkAfterStart` (the one owner of the start check) adds one warning per portal and missing level, `portal <id>: dimension <dim> is not a level of this world; nobody travels there`; at use the same line once per portal and level per server; no teleport.
- `PortalLighting`: lighting with an item plays `minecraft:item.flintandsteel.use` at the clicked frame block (orchestrator's decision after B334); the `light_portal` action plays nothing.
- `MsmPortalTravelGameTest`: 9 GameTests with seven new `portal_travel_*` definitions (each its own vanilla frame block, so no two tests link) and `data/msm_test/function/portal/arrived.mcfunction`. `MsmPortalBlockGameTest`'s sorted-id check leaves the `portal_travel_*` ids out.
- Checks: `./gradlew build` on 26.3 (twice), `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`: 398 GameTests each (389 + 9), 610 JUnit; `./gradlew -p parity build -Pmc=26.3` green.

Decisions
- With `travel.scale`, the scale applies only between `return_to` and `destination`; from a third dimension the dimension types decide.
- `cooldown_ticks` also replaces vanilla's refresh while a cooling entity stands in the portal (otherwise an arrival standing in its exit would leave with vanilla's 300 or 10 ticks and the setting would never be seen).
- Surface arrival counts a fluid as ground (an ocean or lava surface); the feet may not be in lava.

Next
- B339 copies `PortalTravel` and the cooldown refresh into the eject; B341 and B343 check the behaviour on real servers with a project dimension.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B336b surface arrival never lands on lava

**What:** `PortalTravel.surface(...)` no longer treats lava as ground: when the first spot in the column with room above it is a block whose fluid is `#minecraft:lava` (a lava lake or sea), the column is skipped and the result is empty, so travel falls back as before (an exit of `frame_block` is found or built; with no exit block, the traveller lands at the target). Lava enclosed in rock (no room above) is passed over as before. Water stays ground: the traveller stands on its surface. New GameTest definition `portal_travel_surface_nether` (to the Nether, `arrival: surface`, frame `minecraft:red_nether_bricks`, no travel sound); new GameTests `surfaceArrivalNeverLandsOnLava` (a 7 by 7 lava sheet under the target: `surface` is empty, arrival is `PORTAL`, the traveller is neither in nor on lava and an exit is built) and `surfaceArrivalStandsOnWater` (a water sheet: arrival `SURFACE` on the water at y + 1, nothing built); both clear their sheets and exits afterwards. 400 GameTests per variant (26.3, `-Pmc=26.4`, `-PwithoutGeckolib`; 11 in `MsmPortalTravelGameTest`), 610 JUnit.

**Decisions:** "a column whose top is lava" read as the first spot with room for the traveller; lava below solid rock without room above it does not end the scan (a lava pocket in the Nether's roof does not skip the column).

**Next:** B339 copies the lava rule into the ejected `PortalTravel`.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B352 particle options, motion, Script API 1.3, ambient particles

What
- Runtime (ADR 0080 D5, D6): `spawn_particle.particle` is an id or a vanilla options object (`events/ParticleSpecs.Spec`, kept as JSON, decoded with `ParticleTypes.CODEC` through the running world's registry ops, cached per spec and registry access); new `motion` (`[x, y, z]`), `force` and the `count` cap 1000. Every options object is decoded once at `SERVER_STARTED` (`ParticleSpecs.checkAfterStart`, called from `MsmRegistrar.checkAfterStart`): one ERROR per broken object naming the definition, the event and the field; it then sends nothing. Plain ids are still checked while definitions load (`MsmRegistrar.checkParticle`).
- `msm:ambient_particles` is `BlockComponents`' 15th field (one left, limit C18/K14). `registry/AmbientParticles` holds the pure spawn plan; `BlockBehaviourDriver.animateTick` draws it on the client; `MsmBlock` and every family class but `MsmPortalBlock` override `animateTick` (super first, then the driver). On a portal the component is an error and is dropped (`BlockType.allows`). A `states` property the block lacks, or a value it never takes, is a warning.
- Script API 1.3 (`World.spawnParticle(particle: string | ParticleOptions, pos, { count, spread, speed, motion, force })`, alias `ParticleOptions`, "since runtime 1.7.0"); snapshot `script-api-v1-1.6.0.json`; new `script-api-1-3.test.ts`; the 1.1 and 1.2 tests treat `spawnParticle` as widened.
- `ConformanceCorpusTest.PENDING` is empty: `action-particle-` and `ambient-particles-` decode (parseBlock).
- GameTests: `MsmParticleSpawnGameTest` (18): dust (array and integer colours), block (plain id), item (project and vanilla), `motion`, `force`, count 1000/1001, a broken object (one start error, nothing sent), the script forms and errors, the ambient plan with a seeded random (placement, `chance`, a machine's `lit`, nothing on a server level, nothing sent by `animateTick`), portal and `states` problems. New test files `block/particle_spawner.json`, `ambient_*.json`, `particle_bad_*.json`, `script/particles.js`.
- Verified: `./gradlew build` on 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4`, `-PwithoutGeckolib`: 429 GameTests each, 685 JUnit; `./gradlew -p parity build -Pmc=26.3` green; dedicated 26.3 and 26.4 servers with a hand-made jar (a particle, ambient particles on a block, a slab and leaves, a dust object with `motion` and `force`, a block object) pass with 0 errors; with `-verbose:class` no `dev.mcsupermods.runtime.client` class, no `net.minecraft.client` class and not `AmbientParticles` is loaded. Scripting, schemas and target-mc-26.3 tests, lint, typecheck green.

Decisions
- `spread` of `spawn_particle` is vanilla's: a Gaussian offset with standard deviation `spread` on each axis. With `motion` the server draws the same Gaussian offset per particle and sends one count-0 packet each (distance = motion, speed 1), so each particle starts with exactly `motion`; `speed` is not used with `motion`.
- `msm:ambient_particles` `spread` is uniform: `offset + (2r - 1) * spread` per axis (the defaults cover the whole block); `velocity` is exact; `chance` draws one `nextFloat` only when below 1.
- Scripts: `count` above 1000 is a `RangeError` only with `motion` (without it one packet, as before); an options object whose type takes no options may hold no other field (also in the start check).
- `MsmScriptGameTest`'s script count went from 22 to 23 for the new `particles.js` (outside the brief's owner list; no other way to add a script).

Next
- B355 eject mirrors `ParticleSpecs.send` and `AmbientParticles.plan`; mcdoc wording for `spread`/`motion` (orchestrator); the block `block_state` object form `{Name, Properties}` does not decode on 26.3 (only a plain id string was checked).

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B363 Rules format

What
- New `packages/schemas/mcdoc/msm/rules.mcdoc` (ADR 0082 D2, D4, D5, D8): `::msm::rules::RuleBook` (`format: 1`, `rules`, `counters?`), `Counter` (`name`, `scope` player/mob/world, `start?`), `Rule` (`key` 1..32, `name?`, `enabled?`, `when`, `only_if?`, `do` up to 50), `When` (`trigger` enum of the 43 D4 ids, spread over the dispatcher `msm:rule_trigger`, which gives each trigger its `subject` with the right `#[id]` registry and its own `options`), `Conditions` (`match` all/any, `conditions`), `Condition` (`condition`, `not?`, dispatcher `msm:rule_condition`), steps on three levels (`Step`, `NestedStep`, `InnermostStep`; plain steps in `msm:rule_step`, logic steps in `msm:rule_logic_step` and `msm:rule_logic_step_nested`; level 3 takes plain steps only), values (`Value`, `PlainValue` inside `math`, dispatcher `msm:rule_value`), `NumberSlot`, `TextSlot`, `Place`, `Who`.
- `symbols.json` regenerated (257 to 362 types); `MSM_SCHEMA_REFS.rules` = `msm:rules`, `MSM_TYPE_PATHS.rules` = `::msm::rules::RuleBook` and the alias.
- New `packages/schemas/test/rules-schema.test.ts` (127 tests): the ADR example, every trigger with and without a subject, options per trigger, every step, condition and value, caps, three levels accepted and a step nested four deep rejected, unknown ids, references collected with their registries. `tools/build-msm-mcdoc` test lists `rules.mcdoc`.
- Verified: `node tools/build-msm-mcdoc/index.ts --check`, schemas tests (1186), tools test, target-mc-26.3 and 26.4, blocks-items, scripting and core tests, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`.

Decisions

## 2026-11-14 — executor — portals-path save flake

What
- Root cause of the CI failure at `portals-path.spec.ts:533` (runs 43616173662, 43616201056; footer "Unsaved changes", undo "Edit gates:place_portal"): an app bug. The function and script editors hold typing back for 150 ms (`useDebouncedLines`) and Save did not report it, so a Save within 150 ms of the last keystroke wrote the old lines; if the held edit landed while the files were written, `markSaved` even marked the unwritten edit as saved (shown "Saved" with stale files on disk, reproduced locally), otherwise the footer flashed "Saved" and went back to "Unsaved changes".
- Fix: `app/src/renderer/src/session/pending-edits.ts` (`registerPendingEdit`, `flushPendingEdits`); `useDebouncedLines` registers its flush while mounted; `ProjectSession.save` and the discard check report held edits first, and `save` marks the project saved only when the state did not change during the writes.
- Second race found under load (`SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` in `savedBlock`, also reported by B357): `reopenKeepsEdits` in `portals-path` and `machines-path` saved a project that was already saved, so "Saved" was showing before the click and the test read an element file while the no-op Save rewrote it. Fixes: the scoped project file system (`main/platform/scoped-fs.ts`) now writes through a temporary file and a rename (a contained symlink keeps pointing at its replaced file), so nothing ever sees a half written project file, also after a crash; `reopenKeepsEdits` asserts the caller's save instead of saving again; the `save` helpers of those two specs wait for "Unsaved changes" before clicking. `portals-path` also checks the typed function lines reached the saved file.
- Tests: `project-session.test.ts` (held edit saved; edit during the writes stays unsaved; both fail without the fix), `FunctionEditor.test.tsx` (flush on save), `scoped-fs.test.ts` (whole replace, no temp left, write through a contained link).
- Verified: `portals-path` 10 of 10 (20 tests) twice under four busy-loop CPU hogs and with `machines-path` 10 of 10 unloaded; full e2e twice (load average about 30 from other agents): one unrelated dropped input each time (`launchers-path` install menu click, `plugins-path` Escape), each passing 6 and 3 times on rerun; `pnpm --filter @msm/app test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`.

Decisions
- Fixed in the app rather than by raising timeouts; saving unchanged files is kept (rewrites are now harmless).
- The other specs' `save` helpers (creator, families, mobs) have no save of an already saved project and are unchanged.

Next
- Exports and Test in Minecraft read the session state without `flushPendingEdits`: an export within 150 ms of typing uses the old lines (minor; could flush in the export paths too).
- Two saves started back to back are not queued; with atomic writes the later one wins per file, but a session-level queue would be cleaner.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B385 Try it measurements

What
- Measured ADR 0085 D11's gate with a throwaway probe in the scratchpad (not committed): an esbuild bundle of deepslate 0.27.2 `StructureRenderer` over a mutable 48 by 32 by 48 `StructureProvider` (48 by 48 floor plus 2,000 random blocks: 4,304 blocks, `sample-mod` textures on MSM fallback parents) and the app's own `preview/geo/renderer.ts`, `geometry.ts` and `keyframes.ts` drawing twelve `sample-mob` glow golems with `walk`; Electron 45.2.2 under `xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24"` with `--use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`; a first-person camera on a fixed circle, one block placed or removed per frame with `updateStructureBuffers([touched chunks])`. Frame rate from `requestAnimationFrame` over 6 s; CPU per frame from `/proc/<pid>/stat` of every Electron process. No hardware GPU in the container.
- The container was shared with other agents (load average 10 to 37 on 4 cores), so frame rates are pessimistic; CPU milliseconds per frame are the steadier figure.
- Results at 640 by 360, chunk size 8 (medians of 3 to 7 runs): plain `drawStructure` 14 to 20 fps (median about 16), 60 to 92 CPU ms a frame; drawing only the chunk meshes inside the view frustum 20 to 36 fps (median about 24), 49 to 60 CPU ms; the same with the twelve mobs in the shared context and a state reset 19 to 54 fps (median about 23); 320 by 180 with culling and mobs 43 to 47 fps; 960 by 540 8 to 11 fps. Single-block rebuild (own chunk plus neighbours across a boundary): chunk 8 median 1.1 to 1.5 ms, p95 4 to 14 ms; chunk 16 median 8 to 12 ms, p95 20 to 77 ms. Full build 170 to 600 ms (about 270 typical). Blocks as non-opaque (the preview's current `{ opaque: false }` for every block) cost 60 per cent more quads and halve the frame rate.
- Shared context: deepslate and the geo renderer share one WebGL context with no GL error, but the geo pass disables `CULL_FACE` and deepslate enables it only in its constructor, so the next frame differs (checked by a pixel hash) and costs about 20 CPU ms more; re-enabling cull face, blend and depth before deepslate (2 microseconds) gives an identical picture. A stacked second canvas costs about 8 CPU ms a frame more and does not hide mobs behind blocks.
- T9: Electron 45 on this GPU-less machine gives no WebGL without flags (also with `--disable-gpu`); `--enable-unsafe-swiftshader` alone is enough for SwiftShader WebGL. The app's main process sets neither switch today.

Decisions
- Verdict: go, at 48 by 32 by 48, with chunk size 8, per-chunk frustum culling, real opacity flags and the state reset after the mob pass; without the culling it is borderline under SwiftShader on a busy machine. Chunk 16 fails the rebuild threshold.
- Mobs share deepslate's context (no stacked canvas).

Next
- B389: chunk 8, own frustum-culled draw over deepslate's chunk meshes, real `BlockFlags`, a `getBlocks()` scoped to the dirty chunks, rebuild of neighbour chunks across a boundary; B395: reset GL state after the geo pass. Orchestrator: whether main appends `enable-unsafe-swiftshader` (Windows with a blocked GPU still unchecked); a re-measure on a quiet machine and on a hardware GPU.
## 2026-11-14 — executor — B356 client GameTest route

What
- Probe (ADR 0081 D6 (c)): a real 26.3 client runs headless here. Step by step: (1) `enableClientGameTests = true`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x720x24" ./gradlew runClientGameTest`: the client reaches window creation and fails "Failed to create window for OpenGL context: Couldn't find matching GLX visual", then Vulkan "Installed Vulkan doesn't implement the VK_KHR_surface extension" (no Vulkan driver), and hangs (the 24-bit screen alone is not the fix). (2) Cause, found with a ctypes GLX probe: the OpenGL backend asks SDL for 3.3 core with an sRGB-capable framebuffer (`SDL_GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB_CAPABLE` 1, read with `javap`); Xvfb's GLX lists 240 configs and none is sRGB-capable, though the extension strings name `GLX_ARB_framebuffer_sRGB`. (3) `SDL_VIDEO_X11_WINDOW_VISUALID=0x21` gets the window but "Could not create GL context". (4) Installing Mesa's EGL (`apt-get install libegl1 libegl-mesa0`) and `SDL_VIDEO_FORCE_EGL=1`: "Using graphics backend OpenGL, using drivers: 4.5 (Core Profile) Mesa 25.2.8", a singleplayer world opens. 26.4-snapshot-7 tries Vulkan first, then the same OpenGL path.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B367 core project expanders

What
- `@msm/core` applies plugin API 1.15.0 project expanders (ADR 0082 D9): new `src/lowering/expand-project.ts` with `expandProject(project, plugins, target): Promise<ExpandProjectResult>` and `expandProjectSync` (`{ project, origins: Map<string, ElementPatchOrigin>, problems }`), `projectExpanders(plugins)`, `expansionOriginKey(elementId, pointer)` (`<id>#<pointer>`), `originForProblem` and `mapProblemsToOrigins`.
- Every expander gets the saved elements in lowering order; patches apply in plugin, expander and patch order to deep copies of the patched elements' `data` in a structural copy of the project (unpatched elements shared). Paths: strings are object keys, numbers list indexes (0 to the length), missing parent objects are created, an empty path replaces `data` (must be an object); keys are written with `defineProperty`, so `__proto__` is an ordinary key.
- New codes: `core.expansion-conflict` (the same element and path twice; on the later patch's origin, first value kept), `core.expansion-failed` (thrown, rejected or malformed result, or a Promise in the synchronous variant; one error per element of the expander's kinds, or one without an element), `core.expansion-invalid-patch` (unknown element, bad path, origin or value, or a path through a non-container; on the origin).
- `lowerProject` and `lowerProjectAsync` take an optional `options: LowerProjectOptions` (`plugins?`): with it the project is expanded first, expansion problems come first and lowering problems on patched places move to the origin. Without it nothing changes (existing callers untouched).
- Tests: `packages/core/test/expand-project.test.ts` (9): patched data lowered and the saved project byte-identical, structural copy and origins, a `validateJson` problem on a patched field mapped to the rule, plugin order and conflict, saved elements given to every expander, throwing/rejecting/malformed expanders, async versus sync, path rules and refusals.
- Verified: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, full `turbo run test --force --concurrency=4` (22 tasks green).

Decisions
- Expansion is opt-in in the lowering drivers (`options.plugins`): expanding an already expanded project would let an expander read its own patches as saved data (a rules compiler would chain a generated event to itself), so a host that expands once for validation and export passes the expanded project and no plugins.
- A mapped problem keeps code, severity, message and `file`, takes the origin's element and pointer (no `path` for `''`) and loses `range`.
- A patch that cannot be applied gets its own code (`core.expansion-invalid-patch`), not named in the brief.

Next

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B368 Rules plugin

What

- Compiler: `compileRuleBooks(books, elements, target)` compiles every book of a project together; books with rules on the same subject and trigger share the one event `<subject>_rules_<trigger>` (hand-made event first, then each book's part in id order: its plain actions or a `run_script` to its own handler; options from the first book's first rule), and one subject's events and components from several books are one patch each, so core never sees the same path twice. `compileRuleBook` is the one-book case. `ElementPatch` comes from `@msm/plugin-api`; the local copy is gone.
- Lowering: `lower(element, target)` sees one element, but the script needs the whole project, so the expander writes each book's generated lines into the book's expanded copy at `generated_script` (cleared with `null` when a saved book has one by hand) and the kind lowers it to `msm/<ns>/script/rules/<book path>.ts` (layer `msm`, `language: 'typescript'`). A plain, empty or unexpanded book lowers to nothing. F24 confirmed: the content jar transpiles every `msm`-layer `typescript` output (`isScript` in `fabric-content-jar`).
- Script API 1.4 (B370 merged into the branch): "Remove the mob" is `target.remove()` and skips players; "Remove a block" is `world.breakBlock(blockPos(at))` with drops, `{ drops: false }` without; `rules.drops-not-supported` removed; drop counts capped at 64 (`MAX_DROP_COUNT`), weather seconds in (0, 1000000] (`MAX_WEATHER_SECONDS`; 0 or less leaves the length to the game), explosion power clamped to 0..10 for readings too; block places were already block centres. `test/fixtures/script-api-1-4.d.ts` deleted; the type check reads only the real typings (moved into `test/ts-check.ts`). ## 2026-11-14 — executor — B369 runtime dev mode, server side

What
- `engine-mod` gains `dev/` (ADR 0084 D2, D4, D6): `DevMode` (decided per server at `SERVER_STARTING`, before the script host loads; on for a client's integrated server with a valid `<gameDir>/msm-dev/dev.json`, or in a GameTest run (`fabric-api.gametest` set) when `msm.dev.testRoot` names a folder with a `dev.json`; off and reading nothing on a dedicated server; log line `[msm_runtime] dev mode for <namespaces> (singleplayer test world)`), `DevFiles` (read-only parsers of B366's `dev.json` and `setup.mcfunction` sections), `EventOverlay` (`overlay/msm/<ns>/<kind>/<path>.json` for block, item, entity and effect definitions of the session's namespaces: keys left out come from the installed definition, `events` from the overlay, any other key must equal the installed one; the merged file goes through `DefinitionParser`; the map is swapped whole at start and on `END_DATA_PACK_RELOAD`; a refused file logs one error and keeps the events in use, a removed file falls back to the jar's), `DevSetup` (first join of each server run in the test world: setup then refill on a world without the marker, refill only after; marker = persistent overworld attachment `msm_runtime:dev_setup`; lines run as the server at the spawn; unparsable lines are errors, lines that report no success are counted).
- `EventRunner.fire` resolves the overlay first (an empty map without dev mode); `ScriptScanner` adds `overlay/msm/<ns>/script/**.js` in dev mode (same id replaces the jar script in place and keeps its mod; a new id is added); `MsmRuntime` registers `DevMode` before the script bridges.
- Tests: `MsmDevModeGameTest` (5: `decision_only_for_clients_or_the_test_root`, `dev_mode_is_on_for_the_test_root`, `event_overlay_replaces_only_events`, `script_overlay_replaces_the_jar_script`, `setup_runs_once_then_the_refill`), test block `msm/msm_dev_test/block/dev_switch.json`; JUnit `DevFilesTest` (6). `./gradlew build` 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`: 434 GameTests each (was 429), 691 JUnit; `./gradlew -p parity build -Pmc=26.3` green. `tools/run-fabric-server` on 26.3 and 26.4 with `msm-dev/` (dev.json, an overlay, a setup function) in the server folder, `--forbid-line 'dev mode'` and friends: PASS, also with `-Dmsm.dev.testRoot` set; a control run before the GameTest guard logged the dev line and failed as it should.

Decisions
- Fabric's GameTest server reports `isDedicatedServer() == true`, so the test root is honoured only in a GameTest run (`fabric-api.gametest`), never on a plain dedicated server.
- `build.gradle.kts` belongs to particles B356 in this wave, and a GameTest class is first initialised when its first test runs (after `SERVER_STARTING`), so `MsmDevModeGameTest` sets `msm.dev.testRoot` itself (fresh `msm-dev-gametest/` in the run folder) and calls `DevMode.decideFor(server)`, the `SERVER_STARTING` listener, when dev mode is still off.
- No real `/reload` in the automatic run (it resets the scripts other tests use): the tests call `DevMode.dataPackReloaded` and a detached script host, which is what `END_DATA_PACK_RELOAD` runs.
- Overlays apply in any world of the dev instance's integrated server; the setup function only in the world named by `dev.json`. The chests refill once per server run, so a reopen refills too.
- Overlays and scripts outside `dev.json`'s namespaces are ignored with an error.

Next
- B374: client hooks (play request, requests, status); a reopen request also refills the chests.
- B381: forbid `[msm_runtime] dev mode for` on dedicated servers with an `msm-dev/` folder.
## 2026-11-14 — executor — B388 Sim: player (Try it)

What
- New `packages/sim/src/player/`: `constants.ts` (the movement numbers, each commented as an approximation: box 0.6 by 1.8, eye 1.62 (1.27 sneaking), gravity 0.08, vertical drag 0.98, jump 0.42 (about 1.25 blocks), step-up 0.6, walk 0.216 a tick (about 4.3 blocks a second), sneak factor 0.3, flying 0.546 across and 0.375 up and down, reach 4.5, a ceiling 8 blocks above the area), `collide.ts` (`BlockLookup`, the area's invisible walls, floor at y 0 and ceiling, `collectObstacles`, `sweep` y then x then z, `moveWithStep`), `pick.ts` (a ray through the blocks it passes against outline boxes: block, face, hit point relative to the block, world point, distance, box index; `lookDirection`, `faceOffset`, `adjacentPos`), `controller.ts` (`PlayerController` with `step(input)` at 20 ticks a second, `view()`, `interpolatedPosition`, `eyePosition`, `pick`, `wouldOverlap`, `teleport`, `setFlying`), `index.ts`; one export line in `src/index.ts`.
- Tests under `packages/sim/test/player/` (27 new, 28 in the package) with fake `BlockShapes` (full cube, bottom slab, stair, a door's thin box closed and open, a flower without collision): walking speed, a wall, a full block not climbed but jumped onto, a slab and stairs walked up, stepping off a block and landing, a jump of 1.25 blocks within 0.02, flying up, hovering, flying down and landing, toggling flight off, the edge walls and ceiling, the invisible floor, sneaking at about a third without edge safety, interpolation values, overlap with a placed block, a 1,000-tick seeded scripted run giving the same end position twice; pick on a door's lower and upper boxes, an open door's empty part, a slab's top, front and empty upper half, the reach, a block without outline.
- `pnpm --filter @msm/sim test`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` green.

Decisions
- The controller reads blocks through `BlockLookup = (x, y, z) => BlockState | null`, so B387's world plugs in with a one-line adapter; nothing here imports `src/world`.
- Coming down onto the ground ends flying, as in the game's creative flight; flight starts with `toggleFly` and climbs with `jump`, sinks with `sneak`.
- The area is closed by invisible walls at x and z 0 and 48, a floor at y 0 and a ceiling at y 40 (32 plus `CEILING_MARGIN` 8), so a flying player can look down on the area but not leave it.
- Accelerations are derived from the settled speeds (`accelerationFor`), so the constants name speeds that can be checked against the game.
- Pointing visits blocks in the order the ray passes them; an outline box reaching outside its own block is hit only where the ray passes that block. A ray starting inside a box ignores it.
- Biome sorts `src/index.ts`'s exports, so the player line sits above `types.js`.

- B391/B390: the world adapter `(x, y, z) => world.get(...)` and the catalogue as `BlockShapes`.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B391 Sim: clock, growth and tools (Try it)

What
- `packages/sim/src/tick/clock.ts`: `SimClock(onTick)` at 20 ticks a second (`TICKS_PER_SECOND` from `player/constants.ts`, `TICK_MS` 50): `advance(elapsedMs)` runs the ticks that fall due (at most `MAX_CATCH_UP_TICKS` 10, the rest of a long stall dropped), `pause`, `resume`, `step` (one tick, paused or not), `setSpeed` (0.25 to 8, the fast clock), `reset`, getters `tick`, `paused`, `speed`, `alpha` (time between ticks for drawing).
- `timers.ts`: `BlockTimers(world, catalogue)`: `afterUse(pos, useResult)` / `scheduleRelease(pos, ticks)` let a pressed button go after its press time (30 ticks wooden, 20 others, `press_ticks`); `tick(entityBoxes)` presses plates an entity's world box rests on (`PLATE_PRESS_AREA`, a quarter block high) and lets them go 20 ticks (weighted 10) after the last one leaves; weighted plates set `power` by the number of boxes (`weightedSignal`); broken or replaced blocks drop their timers; `clear`, `pending`.
- `growth.ts`: `growBlock` (Grow tool, id `grow`): crop `age` and sapling `stage` one step up; a sapling at its last stage stays and logs "Only in Minecraft: <Name> grows into a tree". `power.ts`: `powerBlock` (Power tool, id `power`): toggles `powered`, else `lit`; otherwise "Only in Minecraft: <Name> has no powered or lit picture; what a redstone signal does to it shows only in the game". `tools.ts`: `applyTool(world, catalogue, log, tool, pos)` and `SIM_TOOLS` (labels Grow, Power).
- `src/index.ts`: one export line. Tests in `packages/sim/test/tick/` (20; package 232).

Decisions
- Plates take plain world boxes (`playerBox(...)` now, mob boxes later). Release delays (20, weighted 10) are approximations of the game's observable timing, held as named constants. A weighted plate's `power` follows the count at once (`ceil(15 * min(n, max) / max)`), rather than only on or off, so its picture matches the game's.
- A crop at its last age logs an ordinary line ("<Name> is fully grown"); a vanilla prop logs "Only in Minecraft: <Name> grows only by the game's own rules". No random ticks; leaves do not decay; nothing travels from a powered block.
- `tools.ts` is a small extra file in the owned `tick/` folder for the dispatcher.

Next
- B390: one `SimClock` in `local-source.ts`; per tick: player step, then `timers.tick([controller.box])`, send the changes as `blockChanged`; after `useBlock`, `timers.afterUse(pos, result)`; a `tool` action calls `applyTool`; `timers.clear()` with "Clear the area". ## 2026-11-14 — executor — B373 Play and Reload service, IPC

What
- New `app/src/main/platform/play.ts` (ADR 0084 D1, D3, D5 to D7, D9): `createPlayService` with `status`, `play`, `reload`, `restart`, `newTestWorld`, `onStatus` and `setPolling`. Play uses only the managed Prism instance `MCSuperMods Test (<mc>)` (created or updated on every Play; the user's install target is never changed). It installs the jar and Fabric API (fetched into the download cache before the game is asked to quit), clears the overlays, the dev resource pack and the world's dev data pack, and writes the dev files: `resourcepacks/msm-dev/pack.mcmeta`, the `options.txt` line, `setup.mcfunction`, `installed.json`, `dev.json` and then `play.json`. It then starts Prism with `--launch`. When the game runs, Play writes a quit request and waits up to 30 s (gone means stale, or the quit handled and no status for 5 s, and the jar installs). Otherwise it stops with "Close Minecraft, then press Play again." Reload hashes the same lowered outputs, classifies them with `classifyChanges`, moves events-only changes of potion, particle and addition kinds to restart, transpiles scripts before writing anything, writes the overlays, `pack.mcmeta` files and `installed.json`'s overlay, and writes a `reopen` or `reload` request (none when nothing is pending). Restart reasons come back in plain words.
- `test-in-minecraft.ts` exports `findPrismRoot`, `checkedFolderInGame` (with an `allowGameDir` option for Play), `realOrNull`, `messageOf` and `LAUNCHER_NAMES`; there is no change in behaviour.

- Tests: `app/test/main/play.test.ts` (12) and the contract samples for the five channels. App suite 176 files, 1614 tests; lint, typecheck and build pass.

Decisions
- Results are `{ ok: false, code, message }` unions instead of thrown errors, so the renderer gets codes (`no-prism` opens the setup panel) without parsing IPC error text.
- Main reads `fabric.mod.json`'s hash and the nested runtime version from the jar (fflate, already bundled). Reload takes the jar optionally; without it, only the mod id is compared.
- The status chip words live in main (`PLAY_STATE_LABELS`, `RESTART_NEEDED_LABEL`). "In another world" is added for a game in a non-test world.
- New test world refuses while the game runs; it renames, never deletes.

Info lines: "You spawned <Name>.", "You hit <Name>; it is gone from the preview.", the cap and no-room refusals, and "<Name> is no longer in the project; it was taken out of the preview."
- No local source was written: `app/src/renderer/src/tryit/local-source.ts` belongs to B390.

One line per id or sprite.
- Frame pictures are found without importing `particle-model.ts` (which pulls the blocks-items plugin into the lazy chunk): `spritePicturePath` takes `TargetFacts.particles.textureFolder` and falls back as the plugin does.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B395 App: mobs in the view (Try it)

What
- New `app/src/renderer/src/tryit/render/mobs.ts`: `MobField({ catalogue, log })` (owner side, pure: `update(snapshots)`, `setCatalogue`, `clear`, `snapshots()`, `size`, `entity(type)`, `revision`, `sayOnce(key, what, { origin?, plain? })`) and `MobPass` (the WebGL side in the view's own context: one look per geo model, texture and animation set, baked once through `preview/geo/geometry.ts`, animations parsed through `keyframes.ts`, drawn through `preview/geo/renderer.ts` with `{ extent: 0 }`; one renderer per look shared by every mob with it; new files bake a look again only when its `.geo.json` or `.animation.json` text changed, and make a new renderer for the picture only when its bytes changed). Helpers: `geoModelFile`, `animationFile` (GeckoLib's layout), `animationNameFor` (`walk` while `walking`, `fly` then `walk` for flyers, else `idle`; a missing walking animation falls back to `idle`), `interpolatedPosition` (partial tick), `turnTowards` (smoothed facing, `TURN_MS` 90), `mobRootMatrix` (feet, `180 - yaw`, `scale / 16`), `writeMobBox`, `writePlate`; `MOB_PLATE_LABEL` "wanders only in the preview", `PLATE_RANGE` 24.
- `TryItCanvas.tsx`: prop `mobs?: MobField | null`; the mob pass draws after the blocks and the outline and before the portal and particle passes, keeping the depth buffer, and the frame then ends with `resetGlForDeepslate`; `partialTick` now also places mobs; `TryItFrameStats` gains `mobs` and `mobPlates`.
- Tests: `app/test/components/tryit/mobs.test.ts` (14: paths, animation choice, interpolation, turning, root matrix facing, box, `MobField`, one bake for 12 mobs, re-bake and re-upload rules, box and lines for a mob without a model and for a missing model file, frustum culling, plates by distance, walk restarting from its start) and `mobs-scene.test.tsx` (1). App suite 197 files, 1817 tests. No `preview/geo/*` file changed.
- Sizes (temporary import, as B389 and B394 measured): `TryItCanvas` 38.9 kB (was 29.8); the geo baker, keyframes and renderer are now a shared 11.1 kB chunk with `GeoCanvas` (8.8 kB); `app.asar` 27.4 MB. Frames under SwiftShader at 640x360 with 4,304 blocks (machine load 7 to 9; noisy): B389's orbit path 50.1 fps without mobs, 46.8 with 12 and 46.6 with 24 (3 to 13 in view); all 24 in view 33 to 42 fps against 34 to 44 without mobs, 24 boxes 37 to 41.

Decisions
- Name plates are textures drawn once per mob name on a 2D canvas (the name over "wanders only in the preview") and shown as camera-facing see-through quads through the particle pass's `QuadBatch`, hidden behind blocks, for mobs within 24 blocks; no plate without a 2D canvas.
- A mob without `msm:animated_model` is a box of its hitbox in MSM's own flat colour, with one "Only in Minecraft" line ("how <Name> looks (it has no geo model); the preview draws it as a box"); a model, animation set or texture the files do not hold, an animation name the set lacks, and a model problem from the baker each give one plain line. An unknown entity type draws a 0.6 by 1.8 box with one line.
- The facing turns smoothly in the view (the snapshot has no previous yaw); positions use `previousPosition` and `position` by the partial tick.
- Models face -z in the baked scene space, so the root turns by `180 - yaw`, as the game's renderers do; not yet checked in the running app against a model with a visible face.

Next
- B390: create one `MobField({ catalogue: entityCatalogue, log })` per area; in the `SimClock` tick call `mobs.update(entities.step())`; pass `mobs={field}` beside `particles` and `partialTick`; on new files call `field.setCatalogue(newEntityCatalogue)`; "Clear the area" calls `field.clear()` after `entities.clear()`. Spawn eggs: hotbar and picker list each `CatalogueEntity` with a `spawnEgg` (name `spawnEggName`); a right click with one calls `entities.spawnFromEgg(itemId, { pos, face })`. The e2e step "spawn a mob, the readout shows one entity, remove it" waits for the view.

Steps: Play makes the managed instance, installs the jar and Fabric API (seeded into the download cache) and the dev files, the stub opens `msm-test-<ns>`, chip "In the test world"; a new function reloads in place ("Reloading 1 change in Minecraft.", the stub handles a `reload` and sees the function in the world's dev data pack, `status.json` `handled` equals its seq); a new block reloads its loot and pictures but shows "Restart needed" with "You added a new block: Play Lamp. …"; Restart writes a quit, the stub stops, Play waits, installs and starts a second stub that opens the world (chip back to "In the test world", the block in the jar); Reload then has nothing to do. About 21 s.
- `app/e2e/modes-path.spec.ts`: the three modes (the row's Very easy shows its toolbar, Home, Things to fix and Play, no sidebar, Problems or target; Easy and Advanced from the row).
- E2e hooks in main (env only, inert otherwise): `MSM_E2E_RUNTIME_DIR` (the runtime jar folder instead of `engine-mod/build/libs/`) and `MSM_E2E_NEW_INSTALL=1` (the launch notice is not suppressed, so a fresh `MSM_HOME` gets the Welcome); `readE2eRuntimeDir`, `readE2eNewInstall` in `e2e-hooks.ts`, used in `index.ts`; unit test in `test/main-e2e-hooks.test.ts`.

Decisions
- The stub is reached without a launcher hook: `PRISMLAUNCHER_DATA_DIR` makes the fake folder Prism's default data folder, and main finds `<root>/prismlauncher` as it would the real program, so the spawn path is the real one. Fabric API is seeded into `<userData>/downloads/fabric-api/<version>/` through `app.evaluate`, so Play never downloads.
- Play and Share need a nested runtime; CI's e2e job has no Gradle build, so `MSM_E2E_RUNTIME_DIR` points at a stand-in jar the test writes.
- Rule menus open popovers that can reach past the window's bottom, so the specs choose entries through their DOM click event.
- The chip problem is checked in the Rule book Studio: the Rules section in a Block Studio shows only compile problems (B375), so an empty item chip is not marked there.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — B396 Sim: triggers and actions

What
- New `packages/sim/src/events/`: `definitions.ts` (`TRIGGER_SPECS`, every trigger field of the format with `handled`, words, cooldown, interval, chance and hand fields; `readEventDefinitions(files, target)` -> `EventDefinitions` of `EventOwner {id, kind, displayName, events, triggers, maxStackSize?, origin}`; `readScripts` reads Rules' `run_script` handlers and their `// rule:<key>` markers and the `msm.events.on` listeners; `ruleBooksFrom`, `rulesForActions`, `ruleEventOf`), `trace.ts` (`SimTrace`, `TraceEntry {tick, kind trigger|action|skipped|onlyInMinecraft, text, origin, trigger?, action?, actionIndex?, depth?}`, `TRACE_LIMIT` 500; every entry also goes to the log), `actions.ts` (`SIM_ACTIONS` for all 13 action types, `runEvent`, `SimInventory` of 9 slots, `parseBlockState`, `soundName`, `MAX_EVENT_DEPTH` 16), `triggers.ts` (`TriggerEngine`, `ChanceMode` random|always|never, `RANDOM_TICK_ODDS` 3/4096).
- `local-source.ts`: the `TODO(B396)` markers wired: `on_interact` (and a container's `on_open`) after the block's own use, `on_use_on_block`, `on_place` after placing, `on_spawn` after a hatch, `on_use` when nothing took the click, `on_break` before breaking, `on_death` after a hit, the Power tool's `on_powered`/`on_unpowered`, and per tick `on_step`, `on_entity_inside`, mob `on_tick` and random ticks. New action `interact` (right-click a mob: `on_interact`). Getters `trace`, `inventory`, `chance`; `setChanceMode`, `setRuleBooks`; options `chance`, `ruleBooks`.
- `types.ts`: `SimEffect` gains kind `animation` and optional `velocity`, `options`, `volume`, `pitch`, `target`, `controller`, `origin`; `SimOrigin` gains `eventId`, `ruleKey`, `ruleBook`; `PlayerAction` gains `interact`. `PlayerController.launch` and `SimEntity.launch` (the `launch` action). `entities/catalogue.ts`: the five entity event components left `COMPONENT_WORDS` (the trigger engine fires or says them). `test/lower-fixture.ts` knows `msm.rules`.
- Tests under `packages/sim/test/events/` (31): the schema walk (`ActionType` in `action.mcdoc` equals `SIM_ACTIONS`; each action fired leaves a trace; the validators' `EVENT_FIELDS` and `definition.mcdoc`'s trigger fields are all in `TRIGGER_SPECS`; every unhandled trigger is said), triggers and actions on a small `ev` project, and Rules through lowering: `fixtures/sample-rules`' "Ring the chime" and "Keep watch" fire with their rule names, the script rules and the library's Rules examples are said with their keys. `@msm/sim` 318 tests; app `test/components/tryit` 99 green.

Decisions
- Clean room: the trigger order follows MSM's own runtime (`BlockBehaviourDriver`, the type block classes, `MsmItem`, `MobDriver`, `EventRunner`, `EventContext`), read only for the order and the `self`/`other` rules; no Mojang code was read.
- The block's own use comes first, then `on_interact`; a sneaking player with something in hand skips the block (secondary use), so a sneak with an empty hand now opens doors (B390 skipped every sneak-use).
- A hit fires `on_death` only (the runtime fires `on_hurt` only when the mob survives); `on_hurt` is said at the first spawn.
- Random ticks are simulated at the game's average odds so `msm:on_random_tick`'s `chance` (the only trigger chance in the format) runs; `always` and `never` decide chances, not the random ticks themselves.
- Plain rule actions are mapped to their rule from the rule books when the view passes them (`ruleBooks`); without them a plain rule's event is named by its trigger. Script rules are named from the generated script's markers.
- Spawned particles are emitted one effect per particle with a seeded spread, so the effects are deterministic.

- B398: wire `effect` events in `session-source.ts` (particles to `ParticleField.emit(options ?? id, {x,y,z,xd,yd,zd}, origin)`, sounds, chips, animations to the mob field), show `source.trace` and `inventory`, pass `ruleBooks` from the session, send `interact` on a right-click at a mob, the "Run every time" option to `setChanceMode('always')`.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — Rules follow-ups: Copy as my own script, kind_schema, section problems

What
- **"Copy as my own script"** (ADR 0082 D7 (d)). `@msm/plugin-rules` `copy.ts` exports `copyRuleBookAsScript(bookId, elements, target)`: the book's generated script (from `compileRuleBooks` over every book) becomes the lines of a new `msm:script` `<book ns>:<book path>_script` (or `_2`, `_3`; also avoids another book's `rules/<path>.ts`), with only the header comment changed; each generated event of the book becomes a hand-made event `<subject id>_script_<trigger>` (or a free variant) on its subject with the same actions, the trigger points at it and the trigger options in force are written onto the component; every rule gets `enabled: false`. Not offered for a missing book, a book with no rule on, or a book with compile errors. App: `studios/rules/copy-as-script.ts` (`planCopyAsScript`, one changeset: create the script, update the subjects with `before`, update the book) and a "Copy as my own script" box in the Rule book Studio (Advanced only; planned on click; the result line, warnings and "Open the script").
- **`kind_schema` for `msm:rules`**: `schema-summary.ts` takes `maxList` and `maxCases` options and has `KIND_SCHEMA_SUMMARY_ALLOWANCES` (`msm:rules`: depth 8, 24,000 characters, lists and cases up to 64; about 18,000 characters) through `kindSchemaSummaryOptions(kind)`, used by the tool executor. Every trigger, step, logic step and condition is listed and every trigger and step case rendered; other kinds keep the defaults. The tool definitions did not change, so no catalogue hash moved.
- **Rules section problems**: `BlocksItemsStudioHost.problems` (App passes the session's `snapshot.problems`); `RulesSection` shows each book's compile problems plus the session's schema and validator problems on the book (`bookProblems`, repeats dropped), so they reach the chips.
- Guides: `rules.md` (new section "Copy as my own script", the limits line), `scripting.md`, `eject.md` no longer say "planned". The `rules.not-in-eject` message already named the button, so it is unchanged. ADR 0082's "Open" list updated.
- Tests: `packages/plugins/rules/test/copy.test.ts` (6: on both targets the project is lowered through `@msm/core` before and after the copy; the Rules script is gone, the copied script has the same lines after the header, the same handlers are defined, and every definition's triggers run the same actions with `trigger_event` followed; free ids; plain books; a second book; refusals), `app/test/copy-as-script.test.ts` (one undo step through the session, no rule events after, Undo byte-identical), `RuleBookStudio.test.tsx` (+2), `RulesSection.test.tsx` (+2), `components/ai-schema-summary.test.ts` (3). `@msm/plugin-rules` 288, `@msm/ai` 90, app 1895 tests in 205 files, all green; e2e `rules-path` green with a new "Copy as my own script" step and Undo; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` pass.

Decisions
- Events are copied as hand-made events (option (a)), not turned into `msm.events.on` listeners (option (b)): definition triggers (an item's use, a random tick, a mob's attack, a container opening) have no script event, plain rules have no handler at all, and `run_script` from the same trigger keeps the runtime's order, cancelling and actors exactly. With the hand-made events and the same handler ids in the copied script, the lowered mod does the same with no Rules script.
- Each copied event holds this book's part only (compiled alone), so other books on the same thing and trigger keep compiling: they now see the copied event as hand-made and run after it. When a book with an earlier id shared the thing and trigger, its part ran first and now runs second; the copy says so in a warning rather than refusing.
- The trigger options written are the ones in force in the whole-project expansion, so another book's later compilation reads the same values (R16: the subject's own win).
- The plugin test uses a stand-in `msm:script` kind: a project reference from `@msm/plugin-rules` to `@msm/plugin-scripting` made `tsc -b` write `.d.ts` files into the scripting plugin's `src/`. The app test runs the real scripting plugin through the session.
- `kind_schema` gets a per-kind allowance rather than larger global bounds, so other kinds' summaries (and their size) do not change.

Next
- Re-enabling a copied book's rules defines its handlers twice (`scripting.duplicate-handler` warns) and its events run twice; a note on the Rule book, or "Copy" removing the rules instead of turning them off, is for the orchestrator to decide.
- The copied script keeps the `// rule:<key>` markers and `const BOOK`; the sim's `readScripts` may still name those rules from the markers (harmless; B398 may want to ignore scripts that are not under `rules/`).

## 2026-11-14 — executor — CI failures on 2c0a7f2, bd5e2b4 and 6b7d6dc

What
- Three CI runs failed; the commits between them passed. All four failures were flaky, none was caused by its commit:
  - `@msm/app` `test/main/play.test.ts` "pushes status changes while polling" (bd5e2b4 and 6b7d6dc: expected "In the test world", got "Starting…"). The Play service pushes status reads without awaiting them, and the test waited a fixed 20 ms for them; on a loaded runner the read was not done, or an earlier read finished after a later one and pushed the older status last. Reproduced 2 times in 10 under CPU load. Fix: `app/src/main/platform/play.ts` `push` numbers each read and drops one that finishes after a newer one was pushed (a real, small race: the bar could show a stale status until the next poll); the test waits for the statuses with `vi.waitFor` instead of 20 ms; new test "pushes the newest status when an earlier read finishes last" holds the first `status.json` read and fails without the fix.
  - `@msm/sim` `test/entities/entity-world.test.ts` "keeps every mob inside it, even spawned in the corners" (2c0a7f2: timed out at 5 s, 6.3 s on the runner, about 330 ms here). It made 72,000 `expect` calls (600 ticks, 24 mobs, 5 bounds). Fix: the bounds are checked in a plain loop and asserted once (`outside` must be empty, the mob count stays at the cap): 37 ms here.
  - `engine-mod (26.3)` on 2c0a7f2 and `engine-mod (26.4)` on 6b7d6dc, step "Headless vanilla server check (sample data pack ...)": `fetch failed` within half a second, before any server started. Node's generic network error, from the one uncached request in that step, Mojang's version manifest (`serverJar`); the same step passed on the other target of each commit and on c3954d7 and af9c6c3. A network blip. Fix: `tools/run-fabric-server/index.ts` `fetchRetrying` (4 tries, waits 1, 2 and 4 s, on network errors, a body cut off while reading, HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx; other statuses fail at once) for every download of the server checks (Mojang's manifest, Fabric's installer list, POMs, `.sha1` files, jars); `describeError` prints an error's causes, so a final failure names the URL and the reason, not just "fetch failed".

## 2026-11-14 — executor — Changeset create then update

What
- Bug: `ProjectSession.applyChangeset` threw "Cannot assign to read only property 'data'" when one changeset created an element and then updated it. Root cause: `commands.addElement` (core) spliced one pre-made copy of the element into the draft on every run. `planChangeItems` runs the commands on a scratch stack, Immer freezes what a run inserts, and the session then replays the same command objects in `stack.execute`; the second run found the frozen copy in the draft, and `setElementData` assigned to it. `setElementData`, `setElementValue` and `setSetting` shared their copied value the same way.
- Fix: `packages/core/src/commands/commands.ts` clones the stored copy at each `apply`, so every run inserts a fresh object. Nothing is unfrozen.
- Tests: `app/test/session-ai-apply.test.ts` (create then update through the session; the saved state is byte-for-byte equal after undo, redo and undo again) and `packages/core/test/edit-commands.test.ts` (commands replayed on a second stack). Both fail without the fix. Core 206 and app 1957 tests, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.

Decisions
- Fixed in core, not the session, because any caller that replays a command hits it. The "Surprise me" `foldItems` workaround is kept.

Next
- None.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — Updater and relaunch audit

What
- Audited the in-app updater end to end (ADR 0018): feed and version check, download, Restart to update, the relaunch, the first launch after a fresh install and after an update, error paths. Most of it was already right (GitHub provider for `MEZTKING/MCSuperMods`, published releases only, `quitAndInstall(true, true)`, What's new once through `lastSeenVersion`, the setting read at every tick, no single-instance lock to refuse the relaunch, unsigned with no `publisherName`). Fixed:
  - `app/src/main/updater.ts`: `allowPrerelease` and `allowDowngrade` off and `disableWebInstaller` on, set explicitly. `finishInstall` answers `installing`, `failed` or `none`: electron-updater reports a missing or unstartable installer through a synchronous `error` event and returns without quitting, which left a running app with no window; `index.ts` now opens the window again with an error box. The download promise of `checkForUpdates` is handled (a failed download was an unhandled rejection in main). Errors after an update was found read "Could not download the update." (not "Could not check"); HTTP 429 or 403 "rate limit" read "GitHub is limiting update checks right now…".
  - Restart to update reports held-back editor typing (`flushPendingEdits`) and the unsaved state synchronously before main closes the windows (`UpdateBanner` `beforeInstall`, `App.tsx`); before, typing within the editors' pause was not yet dirty in main, so the window closed without the prompt and lost it. The banner says "MCSuperMods will close, install the update and open again."
  - `app/src/main/close-guard.ts`: the window close guard, out of `window.ts` and tested; it no longer stacks a second prompt.
  - `app/electron-builder.yml`: `runAfterFinish: true` and `allowElevation: true` explicit, with notes on the install mode, the folder choice and `appId`. `publish-release.yml` checks the exact installer names and that `latest.yml` names the version, the installer and a sha512.
- Tests: `main-updater.test.ts` (options, sync install failure, cancelled prompt keeps the request, download errors, rate limit, handled download promise), `main-close-guard.test.ts`, `main-updater-feed.test.ts` (electron-updater's real `NsisUpdater` against a local `generic` feed: 1.5.2 found, downloaded with the sha512 check and installed with `--updated /S --force-run` then quit; 1.0.0 and 1.5.1 not offered to 1.5.1; a bad sha512, a 404 installer, an empty feed and an unreachable server; the packaging config; Welcome then What's new once), `UpdateBanner.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx` (flush, then `setDirty`, then install). App tests 1975 green; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` pass.
- Docs: ADR 0018 amendment, `app/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/guide/getting-started.md`, HANDOFF "Waiting on the user" item 1 (the Windows steps).

Decisions
- `autoInstallOnAppQuit` stays off: the brief asked for install on quit, but DESIGN Open Question 4, ADR 0018 and the user guide say nothing installs until the user chooses Restart to update. Reported to the orchestrator as a conflict; not changed.
- `oneClick: false` and `perMachine: false` kept: "Only for me" is the default and needs no elevation; electron-builder has no assisted per-user-only mode, and switching to one-click would drop the folder choice. A per-machine or protected-folder install asks for elevation once per update.
- A failed installer start reopens the window rather than relaunching the process, so the error stays visible.

Next
- The Windows check in HANDOFF (install, publish 1.5.2, banner, Restart to update, reopen on the new version with What's new once). The 1.5.1 → 1.5.2 update runs 1.5.1's updater code; these fixes apply from 1.5.2 on.

## 2026-11-14 — executor — Flush held-back typing on every window close

What
- Every close of the main window (the X, File > Exit, Restart to update) is now a round trip: the guard (`app/src/main/close-guard.ts`) holds the close, sends `msm:v1:app:closeRequest` `{ id, op: 'report' }`, and the renderer (`session/close-requests.ts`, wired in `App.tsx` through the new optional `MsmBridge.onCloseRequest`, preload `src/preload/index.ts`) flushes the function, script and rule editors' held-back edits (`flushPendingEdits`) and answers on `msm:v1:app:closeAnswer` whether the project is unsaved. No answer within one second (`CLOSE_REPORT_TIMEOUT_MS`), or a renderer that is gone, falls back to the last `setDirty`. Before, typing within the editors' pause was not yet dirty in main, so the X skipped the prompt and lost it.
- The prompt now offers **Save**, **Discard changes** and **Cancel** (Save is the default). Save asks the renderer to save (`op: 'save'`, up to 60 s) and closes once the project is saved, so Restart to update carries on to the installer; a failed save shows its error in the app and keeps the window open, like Cancel. The `beforeInstall` flush of Restart to update stays.
- Docs: ADR 0018 (a "Flush on every close" item), `app/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/guide/getting-started.md`. `app/tsconfig.node.json` includes `session/close-requests.ts` (a main-side test imports it).
- Tests: `main-close-guard.test.ts` (clean window closes after the report; held-back typing shows the prompt; Save saves then closes; a failed or rejected save keeps it open; Discard; Cancel; the timeout and a gone renderer fall back to the last state; no stacked prompts; `createCloseRequests` matches answers by id, times out and ignores late or malformed answers; Restart to update with a held-back edit: Save, the window closes and `finishInstall` starts the installer), `close-requests.test.ts` (report, save, a failing save, the X within the pause end to end), `App.test.tsx` (the app answers the report with held-back typing as unsaved). App tests 1989 green; e2e `smoke`, `golden-path` and `datapack-path` pass (each closes the app); `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.

Decisions
- A clean window now waits for one round trip before closing (normally a few milliseconds); main cannot know about held-back typing without asking.
- A save that leaves the project dirty (an edit landed while the files were written) counts as not saved, and the window stays open.

Next
- The Windows check: type in a function, close with the X at once, see the prompt and Save; Restart to update with the same.

## 2026-11-15 — orchestrator — Vanilla parity 2 planned

What
- Planned the next vanilla-parity work for the user's rule "anything that can be made in vanilla java should be possible through this app", from the research report's missing-features ranking (ranks 4, 5, 7, 11, 13, 15, 16) and the coverage audit (sections 1.3, 3 and 4.2): ADRs 0094 (twenty block types, waterlogging, weathering and waxing), 0095 (bags and bundles), 0096 (commands, creative tabs, `block.place` and explosion events through the runtime's first Mixins, Script API 1.6, Rules cards), 0097 (vanilla's feature order as a target fact, W-D1 to W-D4), 0098 (trader mobs, villager professions and job sites, mount storage, shoulder pets), 0099 (fluids), 0100 (dimension type and sky editing) and 0101 (Studios, flows, templates, Try it, tests), all Proposed; `docs/PLAN-vanilla-parity-2.md` with facts F1–F36 (javap over the Loom-cached 26.3 and 26.4-snapshot-7 jars and the Fabric API module jars), open facts S1–S14 for three spikes, limits Q1–Q31, rules for every brief (including "never run `git config`"), two batches in fifteen waves and briefs B440–B487 (B434–B439 left free). ROADMAP has an "in planning" section, HANDOFF "Next" and the coverage audit (section 3 and 4.2) point at the plan.

Decisions
- Two batches. Batch 1 "Vanilla blocks and everyday parity" first (block types are the most-requested vanilla gap, beginner-facing and low risk; bags, commands, tabs, the two events and the worldgen order beside them). Batch 2 "Villagers, fluids and skies" after its spikes (traders and professions need a 26.4 POI seam; fluids are the largest API difference yet).
- New block types are `type` values on `msm:block` (ADR 0067's pattern); torches, signs, hanging signs and stems register a generated companion block. Weathering runs vanilla's own `ChangeOverTimeBlock.changeOverTime` on small per-type subclasses, because vanilla keeps its maps for vanilla blocks and 26.4's Fabric API has no `OxidizableBlocksRegistry`.
- Found: Fabric's `addFeature` skips a placed feature the biome's step already has (biome API 20.1.1 and 20.1.6), so W-D3's same-step duplicate is a "does nothing" warning, not the error the audit proposed.
- Found: on 26.4 a liquid is one fluid with a `SOURCE` property built from `Fluid.Properties` (26.3: separate source and flowing fluids), so fluids get a full version seam and a 26.3-only reserve; 26.4 also lacks Fabric's `PoiHelper` and fluid behaviour registry.
- Found: beds are plain blocks in 26.x (no bed block entity; template bed models), so beds need no client code; signs keep vanilla's block entities, and whether a project wood type draws its own sign texture is the first spike question (fallback: the chosen vanilla wood's look).
- The first Mixins (DESIGN §10 policy): `BlockItem.place` and `ServerExplosion.explode`, identical on both versions; no Fabric event exists for either.

Next
- Show the user the eight ADRs' vetoable defaults; then run B440 (spike, second engine-mod executor beside vehicles' B406) and B442 (worldgen order); B441 after vehicles' B408.

Decisions
- No source of format 1 is text-only (`data` and `set` hold either), so ADR 0089 D9's "bar or icons with a text-only source" became `controls.field-not-for-type` (fields another type reads, such as `text` on a bar); `max` counts for bars and icons only.

- The Score counter template alone gives the info `controls.unknown-objective` (no project file creates `points`); with a load function creating it, all six templates together give no problems. Coordinates text shows Y only (one value per element).
- `controls.needs-jar` (vanilla packs) is B415's.
- The HUD validator re-runs on HUD and vehicle changes only (not on function edits), so the app's validator-routing test keeps `minecraft:function` to its fake plugin.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B440 spike: block types, Mixins, commands and bags in the real game

What
- Answered S1–S10 of `docs/PLAN-vanilla-parity-2.md` by observation on 26.3 and 26.4-snapshot-7: throwaway GameTests (14, on the GameTest server) and one client GameTest (singleplayer, then `createServer()`/`connect()`, headless Mesa EGL) over directly registered blocks of the vanilla classes (signs and hanging signs on a registered and an unregistered project `WoodType`, potted plant, berry bush, cake, cocoa, scaffolding, nether wart, stem, bed, sea pickle, candles, vines, ladders, tall flower, layers, torch, weathering blocks), a bag item with three write-back modes, a command, a creative tab and two head-injection Mixins. Spike code deleted afterwards; `./gradlew build` green on both versions. Results, screenshots and a copy of the spike source are in the scratchpad (`b440/`), the findings in the B440 report for the plan's "Notes from implementation".

Decisions
- Go for ADR 0094 D6 (signs with their own look, no client code, no registration): in 26.x signs are block models, so the board is the project's own blockstate and models on vanilla's `template_*sign*` parents; the edit screens read `<ns>:textures/gui/signs/<path>.png` and `<ns>:textures/gui/hanging_signs/<path>.png` of the wood type's name. Same on both versions, registered or not. D6b is not needed.
- Go for `scaffolding` (D1) with overrides, no Mixin: vanilla's distance counts only vanilla scaffolding and the item's extending only works on vanilla scaffolding, so the driver needs its own distance and item.
- Go for the Mixin route (ADR 0096 D3): both head injections apply and run on the GameTest server, singleplayer and a dedicated server on both versions, no refmap, `compatibilityLevel` `JAVA_25`; cancel and keep-blocks behave as the ADR says.
- Measured vanilla berry harvests: 1–2 at age 2 and 2–3 at age 3 (the fixed loot table `minecraft:harvest/sweet_berry_bush`, which gives sweet berries for any bush and the age-3 bonus only to vanilla's bush).
- Bags: the ADR 0095 D3 guard (locked slot, same-stack `stillValid`, write on every change) closed every route tried; the naive write-at-close menus duplicated on most routes.

Next
- The main session copies the report's "Notes for the plan" into the plan; B441 and Wave 1 may start (B441 still after vehicles' B408).

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B411 runtime: channel and key binds

What
- The runtime's networking channel (ADR 0088 D1, D2): `net/MsmNetworking` registers the serverbound `msm_runtime:key_v1` (`KeyPayload {key, pressed}`: an id of at most 256 characters, one boolean) and the clientbound `msm_runtime:hud_v1` (`HudPayload {hash, values[≤64] {index, number?, text? ≤256, visible?}}`, codec only, for B416) and the server's key receiver. Anything over the bounds fails in the decoder, which vanilla turns into a disconnect.
- `net/InputGuard` (D7 rules 1, 2): a token bucket of 20 packets a second with a burst of 40 per player, drops counted per reason (unknown key, dead, sleeping, spectator, rate limit) and logged at most once a minute per player as `dropped N key packet(s) from <name>: <reason>`.
- `loader/KeyBindDefinition` and `KeyBindParser` (closed Codecs, B409's fields and defaults: unbound is `key.keyboard.unknown`, `category` default `keys`, `hold_interval_ticks` 10); undeclared trigger events are errors, `play_animation` is dropped, `vehicle` without `in_vehicle` or `driving` is ignored with a warning. `ConformanceCorpusTest` decodes `key-bind-` (18 cases).
- `controls/KeyBinds` and `HeldKeys` (D3, D4, D7): press, release and hold events with the player as self, other and actor (`EventContext.forItem`, so `run_function` runs as and at the player at function permission level), `when` and `cooldown_ticks` checked at press time, `while_held` every interval from one interval after the press, the held set cleared without events on leave, death, respawn and dimension change. The runtime keys `msm_runtime:vehicle_fire`, `vehicle_fire_second`, `vehicle_horn`, `vehicle_descend` (R, V, H, Left Alt; pinned against both targets' `runtimeKeys` by `RuntimeKeysTest`) are accepted only when a vehicle type is loaded. `KeyBinds.KeyListener` tells later code (B417, B421) about presses and releases after the definition's events.
- Client: `client/controls/ProjectKeyMappings` (one `KeyMapping` per definition, name `key.<ns>.<path>` with `/` as `.`, category `<ns>:<category>`), `RuntimeKeys` (category `msm_runtime:vehicles`, "MSM Vehicles", only with a vehicle type) and `ControlsClient` (sends down and up edges at the end of each client tick, a one-tick tap as press plus release, every held key's release when a screen opens, the window loses focus or the player leaves). `VehicleDriver.descend` now reads "Vehicle: descend". Lang `assets/msm_runtime/lang/en_us.json` for the four keys and the category. `EventOverlay` lists `key_bind` among the kinds whose events reload in dev mode.
- Tests: JUnit 820 (`KeyBindParserTest` 8, `InputGuardTest` 8, `RuntimeKeysTest` 2, corpus +18); GameTests 559 per variant (`MsmKeyBindGameTest` 14 replacing the placeholder) green in `./gradlew build` on 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`; client GameTests green on both versions (`MsmControlsClientGameTest`: the mappings in Controls with their names, categories and translations, then on a dedicated server a held key runs its press and release functions as the player, a one-tick tap sends press and release, "Vehicle: fire" is held on the server, and opening the chat sends the release); `./gradlew -p parity build` green.

Decisions
- Releases skip the dead, sleeping and spectator checks (only presses are dropped for the player's state), so a key never stays held on the server because the player went to bed with it down.
- A second press of a held key and a press that fails `when` or the cooldown do nothing; only a press that fires holds the key, so `on_release` and `while_held` follow only such a press.
- Key events use the item event context (source ITEM): the player is self and other, offsets from the block below the player.
- The mock GameTest player's game mode is fixed and it does not die from damage, so the spectator rule is covered by the sleeping rule's path and death by Fabric's death event with no health; the real paths run in the client GameTest's dedicated server.

Next
- B416 sends and receives `HudPayload`; B417 reads `HeldKeys.isHeld(player, RuntimeKey.FIRE.id())` or a `KeyBinds.KeyListener`; B418 reads `RuntimeKeys.isFireDown()` and the others; B421 adds the script events `key.pressed` and `key.released` through `KeyBinds.addListener`.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B416 Runtime: HUD

**What**
- HUD elements in the runtime (ADR 0089 D1 to D6). `loader/HudDefinition` (closed Codecs; `HudValue` by `source` data, score, vehicle, player, set; `max` a number or a value; colours `#rrggbb` decode to RGB, anything else is an error) and `HudParser` (format check; `vehicle` without an `in_vehicle` or `driving` show is ignored with a warning; `icons` without `icon` warns; `parseAll` sorts by id as a string). Actions `show_hud`, `hide_hud`, `set_hud` (closed; `value` a finite number or a text of at most 256 characters) in `events/Action.java`, run through `HudServer.action` from `EventRunner`.
- `hud/`: `HudServer` (definitions in index order, the id list's hash, `show`, `hide`, `set` for actions, scripts and Rules, a start-up warning for HUD actions naming an unregistered element, one error per unknown id at run time, one log per owner for actions without a player), `HudValues` (the server's values: script data of the player or world, scores of `@s` or a fixed holder, vehicle fuel, health, ammunition, reload `readyAt - gameTime`, speed from how far the vehicle moved), `HudSync` (every 5 ticks, plus at the end of a tick in which an action changed something; only changes; 64 entries a payload; a clear is an entry with no number, text or visibility; a server-computed `max` has its own slot `count + index`; respawn and dimension change resend everything; leaving forgets), `HudState` (a viewer's slots; payloads of another hash are ignored with one warning).
- Client: `client/hud/HudClient` (the `hud_v1` receiver, cleared on join and leave; the layer `msm_runtime:hud` before chat, registered when there are HUD elements or vehicle types), `MsmHudLayer` (visibility, `player` stats read on the client, text templates with a translation and `{value}`/`{max}`, bars with colours or sprites, icon rows), `HudLayout` (pure layout, fills and number text), `VehicleDashboard` (health, fuel, one row per weapon with ammunition and a reload bar, in the `bottom_right` stack). Seams `client/HudRegistration` for 26.3 (`HudElement` lambda, `RenderPipelines.GUI_TEXTURED`) and 26.4 (`HudElement` object, `GuiPipeline.TEXTURED`).
- `fixtures/hud-layout/golden.json` and its README (the anchor table, constants, 19 elements on 10 screens, bar fills, icon rows, number texts), written by `HudLayoutGoldenTest` with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`. `EventOverlay` lists `hud` as needing a restart.
- Tests: JUnit `HudParserTest` 7, `HudLayoutTest` 6, `HudLayoutGoldenTest` 1, the corpus now decodes `hud-`, `action-hud-` and `vehicle-tank` (917 JUnit in all); `MsmHudGameTest` 10 (583 GameTests per variant, all green on 26.3, 26.4 and without GeckoLib); the HUD half of `MsmControlsClientGameTest` (a colour bar, a sprite bar and a text found inside their boxes, the GUI size rule, the tank's dashboard half full) passes on both versions; screenshot `scratchpad/shots/64-hud.png`. `./gradlew -p parity build` green.

**Decisions**
- Server-computed `max` values use their own payload slots (`count + index`) rather than a new payload field; `hud_v1` is unchanged.
- An entry with no number, text or visibility clears a value (a vehicle stat on foot, removed script data).
- `player` stats on the client: air on the scale of health (0 to 20), x, y and z as block coordinates. A `max` read from a value is 20 until it has a number. Numbers show with at most two decimals.
- Layout constants: margin 2, gap 2, `above_hotbar` stack ending 52 GUI pixels above the bottom; every anchor stacks. The dashboard sits in `bottom_right` below project elements. Vanilla hides HUD layers with F1; nothing more is hidden.
- Dashboard labels use `Component.translatableWithFallback` (`hud.msm_runtime.health`, `fuel`), so the runtime's lang file (B411's) is untouched.

**Next**

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B449 runtime: waterlogging, weathering and waxing

**What**
- Components `msm:waterloggable {}`, `msm:weathering {next?, stage}` and `msm:waxable {into}` in `components/BlockComponents` (closed Codecs; a nested group `AGEING`, since the first group holds 15 of 16 fields). `BlockType.allows`: waterloggable only on `WATERLOGGABLE_TYPES` (block, pillar, horizontal, directional), weathering and waxable only on `WEATHERING_TYPES` (those four plus slab, stairs, door, trapdoor, pane, chain, lantern). `BlockComponents.checkAgeing` (called by `DefinitionParser.parseBlock`): the three components on a container or machine are warnings and not applied (Q8); `msm:waxable` without `msm:weathering` is an error and not applied.
- `registry/types/MsmWaterloggedBlock` (`MsmBlock` plus `SimpleWaterloggedBlock`: `waterlogged` state, placed in water starts waterlogged, schedules the water's tick on shape updates, holds a still source; `canPlaceLiquid` is vanilla's). `registry/Waterlogging.blockFor` replaces B441's stub.
- `registry/weathering/`: `Weathering` (the `Ageing` interface over vanilla's `ChangeOverTimeBlock<WeatherState>`: age, `getChanceModifier` 0.75 at the unaffected stage, `getNext` with the shared properties copied; `blockFor` replacing the stub; the random tick calls vanilla's own `changeOverTime`; `replace` turns both halves of a door; `Maps.build`, pure, with the load errors), `Waxing` (honeycomb waxes, an axe unwaxes or scrapes; only project blocks), and the classes `MsmWeatheringBlock` (+ `.Waterlogged`), `MsmWeatheringSlabBlock`, `MsmWeatheringStairBlock`, `MsmWeatheringDoorBlock` (the upper half follows the lower one through `updateShape`), `MsmWeatheringTrapDoorBlock`, `MsmWeatheringPaneBlock`, `MsmWeatheringChainBlock`, `MsmWeatheringLanternBlock` (subclasses of the B445/B446 classes).
- `BlockExtras`: one use callback, honeycomb first, then the axe (shield rule, then stripping, then `Waxing.axe`); `apply` records each project block for waxing; `copyProperties` is public. `MsmRegistrar`: one line, `Weathering.checkAfterRegistration(errors)` after the stairs and potted plants, and the hook comment.
- Tests: `MsmWeatheringGameTest` 10 (placing in water and both buckets, water flowing out when broken, containers and slabs, the rate beside vanilla copper, mixed neighbours, every type ageing with its state, honeycomb, axe, creative, load errors) on 33 test definitions `weathering_*` and `waterlog_*`; JUnit `WeatheringMapsTest` 7; `ConformanceCorpusTest`: `waterlog-` and `weathering-` decoded (17 cases). `MsmSpikeGameTest`'s allow-list takes `waterlog_slab.json` and the `msm_test:weathering_` link errors.
- Checks: `./gradlew build` on 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`: 913 JUnit, 593 GameTests per variant; `./gradlew -p parity build`.

**Decisions**
- Measured rates over 20,000 forced random ticks with one seed: project tin 0.0436 and vanilla copper 0.0436 (unaffected), 0.0576 and 0.0576 (exposed); a lower-stage neighbour of either kind gives 0 in both directions; three same-stage neighbours of either kind give 0.00275; a waxed copy is no neighbour. `getNextState` alone skips vanilla's base chance, so the random tick uses `changeOverTime`.
- Weathering on a container or machine is dropped with a warning, as waterlogging (the block entity class cannot also be a weathering class); the brief named only waterlogging.
- A `next` cycle, an unknown `next`, two blocks ageing into one, an unknown `into`, a waxed copy that weathers and two blocks waxed into one are load errors that leave the link out; the blocks still register. Vanilla caches `isRandomlyTicking` before the check, so a refused block may still get random ticks; it never ages.
- Wax on plays vanilla's level event 3003 only (no separate sound packet, as the honeycomb); scrape and wax off play `item.axe.scrape` / `item.axe.wax_off` and the level events 3005 / 3004. The wax-on sound on the client is not measured here.

**Next**
- B457: the eject needs a `BlockWaxing` equivalent (the use callback and the maps). B462: the fixture follows the `weathering_*` test set. B463: the time-lapse uses the measured rates. Guide limits for B467 in the report.
